audit_scope.description: This batch covers CL proposer-builder separation (EIP-7732 ePBS with PTC), EL contract creation collision detection (EIP-684), CL-to-EL beacon root bridge (EIP-4788), Dencun fork activation meta-EIP (EIP-7569), EL SELFDESTRUCT opcode alias (EIP-6), JSON-RPC eth_symbol API (EIP-3014), EL gas refund reduction (EIP-3529), wallet silent signing permissions (EIP-5345), EL ecrecover precompile (Cancun), and CL validator activation churn limit (EIP-7514).

out_of_scope: Full EVM opcode implementation beyond collision/refund/ecrecover
Full beacon state transition beyond ePBS/churn/fork mechanisms

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions targeting contract creation collisions, exploit eth_symbol for network identity spoofing, resource exhaustion attacks
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with crafted beacon roots, exploit fork activation boundary edge cases

el_vectors.entry_point: EVM Precompile Call (ecrecover address 0x01), CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes
el_vectors.threat: Craft malformed ecrecover inputs, attempt address collision via CREATE2, exploit gas refund mechanics for economic advantage

cl_vectors.entry_point: P2P Network (Beacon API / gossip, execution payload headers)
cl_vectors.threat: Builder equivocation (conflicting payloads), PTC vote manipulation, proposer-builder collusion for payload reorgs, manipulate churn rate
Provide incorrect payload data, manipulate builder bid selection, denial of service on payload reveal

misclassified_entities.reason: Beneficiary address in EIP-6 SELFDESTRUCT is a passive recipient, not an entity sending data into the system. It is a parameter of the opcode, not an external data source.
Smart contract developer in EIP-6 interacts at compile time, not at runtime. The compiler is a build-time tool, not a runtime external entity sending data into the EVM.
The blockchain network in EIP-5345 is the system itself, not an external entity. Transactions are broadcast TO the blockchain, which is the target system.
Duplicate of EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER in EIP-4788. The beacon chain is the same entity as the consensus layer providing roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Staked Builder via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (signed execution payload headers and envelopes)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builders submit bids and reveal payloads over the P2P network. Despite being staked, builder equivocation has no slashing penalty, so payload content and timing are untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: PTC Member via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: PTC members are validators attesting to payload timeliness via P2P. Individual attestations are untrusted; only aggregate threshold (256/512) provides confidence.

trusted_external_entities.name: Colluding Proposer Set via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (beacon blocks for consecutive slots)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Proposers controlling consecutive slots with >20% stake can attempt payload reorgs. Fully adversarial model.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any EOA or contract can initiate contract creation. No authentication beyond valid transaction signature. Deployer may be malicious, attempting address collision attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL provides beacon block roots embedded in EL block headers. Authenticated via JWT on Engine API. However, content (the root itself) is accepted without independent EL verification - trust is inherited from CL consensus.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM Call
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL to beacon roots contract (0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02) and ecrecover precompile (0x01)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can call the beacon roots contract or ecrecover precompile. Input data is completely untrusted and must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/DApp Client via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet clients query node via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. The response itself is informational and can be spoofed by a malicious node.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Node Operator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators control the eth_symbol response. A malicious node can return false symbol data to deceive users about network identity. No on-chain verification possible.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet Silent Signing API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps request silent signing permissions from wallets. Fully untrusted - may be malicious or compromised. Permission scope and secret validation are the only controls.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Depositor via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone can deposit 32 ETH to queue a new validator. Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials) is untrusted input that must be validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Builder BLS signature must be verified. Bid value must be validated against builder's beacon balance. Blockhash commitment must be well-formed. Builder equivocation (multiple headers for same slot) must be tolerated without consensus failure.

Full multi-stage validation required: BLS signature, blockhash match against committed header, execution state transition validity, withdrawals root match, beacon state root match. Any failure must reject the envelope.

PTC member must be in the assigned PTC for the slot. Attestation signature must be verified. Individual attestations do not determine payload status - only aggregate threshold (>=256/512) is authoritative.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip (beacon blocks for consecutive slots)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork choice must resist reorg attempts by proposers with >20% stake controlling consecutive slots. Unconditional proposer payment (deducted at commitment time) is the primary safety property.

Full collision detection required before init code execution: target address nonce must be 0 AND code length must be 0. Collision triggers invalid opcode exception consuming all gas and reverting state.

EL trusts CL-provided beacon root without independent verification. Root is stored via system call to beacon roots contract. Content validation relies entirely on CL consensus integrity. Ring buffer index (timestamp % 8191) must prevent stale data access via timestamp matching.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM CALL to beacon roots contract and ecrecover precompile
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Beacon roots contract: input must be exactly 32 bytes, non-zero, and timestamp must match stored timestamp at computed index. Ecrecover: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs return empty output (no revert). Callers must handle empty return correctly.

Read-only informational endpoint with no consensus implications. Response format validation only (valid JSON-RPC string). No content verification possible - wallets should cross-reference with chain ID.

Node operator controls response content. Symbol cannot be verified against any authoritative source. Wallets must treat as informational only and not rely on it for security-critical network identification.

Permission request must display full scope to user (chain ID, contract, functions, duration). Permission secret must be cryptographically random (>=128 bits entropy). Every silent transaction must verify: (1) secret matches, (2) permission not expired, (3) transaction within permitted contract/function scope. Secret leakage enables unauthorized transactions until expiry.

Deposit amount must be exactly 32 ETH. Validator pubkey and withdrawal credentials must be valid. Activation rate bounded by MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT (8) to prevent exponential validator set growth. Queue ordering is FIFO.
